meanings.usage: 修饰形容词或分词，表示程度
常用于被动语态，表示颜色深浅
描述人具有敏锐的观察能力
指有香味的产品或气味
描述非常奇特、不寻常的事物
形容行为或要求过于极端
描述虚构的、不真实的东西
指混合多种东西制成的物品

examples.en: He keeps a large bottle on permanent display in his study.
examples.zh: 他在书房里永久陈列着一个大瓶子。

examples.en: Despite the fact that the bottle is tinted green, an observant visitor would notice it's filled with greyish substance.
examples.zh: 尽管瓶子被染成绿色，敏锐的来访者会注意到里面装的是灰色物质。

examples.en: When Harry put on his act of being mildly annoyed, the assistant promised to order some for him.
examples.zh: 当哈利装出有点烦恼的样子时，店员答应为他订购一些。

examples.en: The woman's eyes immediately lit up and she fetched several bottles.
examples.zh: 那女人的眼睛立刻亮了起来，拿出了好几个瓶子。

examples.en: He beat a hasty retreat, clutching the precious bottle under his arm.
examples.zh: 他匆忙撤退，腋下夹着那个珍贵的瓶子。

examples.en: He was glad to get away with a mere twenty pounds.
examples.zh: 他很高兴只花了二十英镑就买到了。

examples.en: He is fond of relating this interesting story.
examples.zh: 他喜欢讲述这个有趣的故事。

examples.en: He would invent fanciful names on the spot.
examples.zh: 他会当场编造一些稀奇古怪的名字。

examples.en: None of them met with Harry's requirements.
examples.zh: 没有一个能满足哈利的要求。

examples.en: How Harry came into the possession of this outlandish stuff makes an interesting story.
examples.zh: 哈利是如何得到这种稀奇古怪的东西的，这本身就是一个有趣的故事。

grammar.title: 过去完成进行时 (Past Perfect Continuous Tense)
grammar.definition: 表示在过去某一时刻之前一直在进行的动作，强调动作的持续性和未完成性 用于描述持续到过去某一点的习惯性动作

examples.en: He had been developing a bad habit for years.
examples.zh: 他多年来一直养成一个坏习惯。

grammar.title: if虚拟条件句（与现在事实相反）
grammar.structure: If + 主语 + were to + 动词原形...
grammar.definition: 表示与现在事实相反或不太可能发生的情况 用于假设不太可能发生的事情

examples.en: If you were to ask Harry what was in the bottle, he would tell you that it contained perfumed mud.
examples.zh: 如果你问哈利瓶子里是什么，他会告诉你里面装的是香水泥。

grammar.title: 间接引语（陈述句的转换）
grammar.definition: 将直接引语转换为间接引语时，人称、时态、时间状语等需要相应变化 叙述他人说过的话时使用，that可省略

examples.en: He said (that) the bottle contained perfumed mud.
examples.zh: 他说瓶子里装的是香水泥。

patterns.pattern: If you were to do..., would/could/might + 动词原形...

original.en: If you were to ask Harry what was in the bottle, he would tell you that it contained perfumed mud.
original.zh: 如果你问哈利瓶子里是什么，他会告诉你里面装的是香水泥。

imitations.en: If you were to visit China, you would learn a lot about its culture.
imitations.zh: 如果你要去中国旅游，你会学到很多关于中国文化的知识。

imitations.en: If you were to practice speaking English every day, you could improve quickly.
imitations.zh: 如果你每天练习说英语，你就能快速进步。

patterns.pattern: Despite the fact that + 从句...

original.en: Despite the fact that the bottle is tinted a delicate shade of green, an observant visitor would soon notice that it is filled with what looks like a thick, greyish substance.
original.zh: 尽管瓶子被染成淡绿色，敏锐的来访者很快就会注意到里面装的是看起来像浓稠的灰色物质。

imitations.en: Despite the fact that he is very young, he speaks English fluently.
imitations.zh: 尽管他很年轻，他的英语说得很流利。

imitations.en: Despite the fact that it was raining heavily, we went hiking.
imitations.zh: 尽管雨下得很大，我们还是去徒步了。

patterns.pattern: 主语 + love/like + to be told that...

original.en: He loved to be told that one of his imaginary products was temporarily out of stock.
original.zh: 他喜欢听别人说他想象中的产品暂时缺货。

imitations.en: She loves to be told that her cooking is delicious.
imitations.zh: 她喜欢听别人夸她的厨艺好。

imitations.en: Children love to be told that they are clever.
imitations.zh: 孩子们喜欢听别人夸他们聪明。

original.en: How Harry managed to keep a straight face during these performances is quite beyond me.
original.zh: 哈利在这些表演中是怎样忍住不笑的，我实在想不通。

imitations.en: Why she married him is quite beyond me.
imitations.zh: 她为什么嫁给他，我实在想不通。

imitations.en: How he passed the exam is quite beyond me.
imitations.zh: 他是怎么通过考试的，我实在想不通。

translation:
我的堂兄哈里在他的书房里一直摆着一只形状古怪的大瓶子。尽管那只瓶子呈淡绿色，但细心的客人很快就会发现瓶里装的是一种看上去黏稠，颜色发灰的东西。要是你问哈里瓶里装着什么，他会告诉你是香水泥。如果你表示怀疑或惊奇，他会立即请你闻一闻，然后取出一些抹在你的皮肤上。这一简单的试验会消除你可能存有的一切疑虑。瓶里装的的确是香水泥。哈里如何得到这种稀奇古怪的东西的，这里有个有趣的故事，而且他挺爱把它讲给别人听。此外，得到这瓶香水泥还治好了他多年的一个坏习惯。
哈里曾认为走进一家名贵化妆品商店，荒唐地提出要买一种根本不存在的商品是件开心的事儿。他会当场编造出一些稀奇古怪的货名。他走进商店后，会提出要一种名叫“香影”的新型香水或什么“不溶浴皂”。要是女售货员告诉他从未听说过这些东西，他会装出十分遗憾和不安的样子。他爱听售货员说他想像出来的那种东西暂时脱销，于是他就煞有介事地许诺改天再来光顾。当然，他再也不会来了。我实在想像不出哈里在这些表演中是怎样装出一本正经的样子的。
毋须暗示哈里就会向你讲起他买下那瓶珍贵香水泥的经过。一天，他去伦敦一家高级商店要买一种叫“密诺莱特”的东西，店员露出诧异的神色。哈里又慢慢地，一字一顿说了一遍这个词，那个女售货员还是迷惑不解地摇了摇头。哈里便进一步解释“密诺莱特”是一种质地坚硬、状似琥珀的东西，可以用来除去雀斑。他的解释显然对女售货员有些启示。她一个货架接着一个货架地寻找，拿出各种各样稀奇古怪的化妆品，但没有一样能够符合哈里的要求。哈里装出不高兴的样子时，女售货员答应为他定货。哈里为他的骗术而感到洋洋得意，又提出要买香水泥。他原想女售货员会惊奇地望着他，不知所措，没料到这回该轮到他自己吃惊了。因为那女售货员听完哈里的话后，马上眼睛一亮，拿出几瓶东西放在柜台上让哈里挑选。哈里只好认输。他挑出一个看上去最小的瓶子，谨慎地问了价。他庆幸自己只破费了20英镑便得以脱身。他把那宝贵的瓶子放在腋下夹着，溜之大吉。从那以后，他认识到自己发明的小小恶作剧是要付出很大的代价的。在他书房的书柜里摆着那瓶形状古怪的香水泥就是他第一次也是最后一次购买的稀有化妆品。

text.title: Mud is mud 实事求是

lines.en: My cousin, Harry, keeps a large curiously-shaped bottle on permanent display in his study.
Despite the fact that the bottle is tinted a delicate shade of green, an observant visitor would soon notice that it is filled with what looks like a thick, grayish substance.
If you were to ask Harry what was in the bottle, he would tell you that it contained perfumed mud.
If you expressed doubt or surprise, he would immediately invite you to smell it and then to rub some into your skin.
This brief experiment would dispel any further doubts you might have.
The bottle really does contain perfumed mud.
How Harry came into the possession of this outlandish stuff makes an interesting story which he is fond of relating.
Furthermore, the acquisition of this bottle cured him of a bad habit he had been developing for years.
Harry used to consider it a great joke to go into expensive cosmetic shops and make outrageous requests for goods that do not exist.
He would invent fanciful names on the spot.
On entering a shop, he would ask for a new perfume called ' Scented Shadow' or for 'insoluble bath cubes'.
If a shop assistant told him she had not heard of it, he would pretend to be considerably put out.
He loved to be told that one of his imaginary products was temporarily out of stock and he would faithfully promise to call again at some future date, but of course he never did.
How Harry managed to keep a straight face during these performances is quite beyond me.
Harry does not need to be prompted to explain how he bought his precious bottle of mud.
One day, he went to an exclusive shop in London and asked for 'Myrolite', the shop assistant looked puzzled and Harry repeated the word, slowly stressing each syllable .
When the woman shook her head in bewilderment, Harry went on to explain that 'myrolite' was a hard, amber-like substance which could be used to remove freckles .
This explanation evidently conveyed something to the woman who searched shelf after shelf.
She produced all sorts of weird concoctions , but none of them met with Harry's requirements.
When Harry put on his act of being mildly annoyed, the assistant promised to order some for him.
Intoxicated by his success, Harry then asked for perfumed mud.
He expected the assistant to look at him in blank astonishment .
However, it was his turn to be surprised, for the woman's eyes immediately lit up and she fetched several bottles which she placed on the counter for Harry to inspect.
For once, Harry had to admit defeat.
He picked up what seemed to be the smallest bottle and discreetly asked the price.
He was glad to get away with a mere twenty pounds and he beat a hasty retreat, clutching the precious bottle under his arm.
From then on, Harry decided that this little game he had invented might prove to be expensive.
The curious bottle, which now adorns the bookcase in his study, was his first and last purchase of rare cosmetics .

lead.summary: 《实事求是》我的堂兄哈里在他的书房里一直摆着一只形状古怪的大瓶子。尽管那只瓶子呈淡绿色，但细心的客人很快就会发现瓶里装的是一种看上去黏稠，颜色发灰的东西。语法聚焦：现在完成时与现在完成进行时、形容词、相应的副词及其用法。

lead.question: Why did Harry decide to give up his little game?
